1) Please attach the withholding certificate (tax authority letter or customer certification) when available.
2) Can you confirm whether BrightWave will remit the withheld amount to the tax authority on our behalf (and provide a remittance schedule), or whether you expect Redwood to claim a credit/refund locally?

- Post the net cash receipt against invoice 20270429 immediately.
- Create a contra receivable (withholding receivable) for the withheld amount so the invoice is not left in unapplied status.
- If we receive the tax certificate and proof of remittance from BrightWave, we clear the withholding receivable and write a journal to reclassify into tax receivable or recognize as adjustment depending on local treatment.

Folks — quick technical note from the ledger side. We should avoid leaving the invoice open for the full gross amount if cash has been received. My suggested bookkeeping steps: 

1) Post cash receipt: Debit Bank SGD 44,700; Credit AR invoice 20270429 SGD 44,700.
2) Create a withholding receivable (AR - WHT receivable) for SGD 2,853 (6% of gross 47,553). Debit WHT Receivable SGD 2,853; Credit AR invoice 20270429 SGD 2,853 — this nets the invoice to zero on the AR ledger.
3) Hold WHT receivable in a separate AR bucket pending receipt of official certificate and remittance evidence.
4) If BrightWave remits to tax authority and provides proof: write WHT Receivable off and record either a tax recoverable (if refundable to us) or record as expense/credit memo depending on counsel advice (we should get tax counsel input).

Attached is a quick payment export showing the bank trace and reference. If we do a credit memo instead, we risk changing revenue recognition mapping — better to keep as receivable until resolved.

Attachment: payment-export-0429.csv

Marcus
Accounting Manager, Revenue & AR

Thanks for the certificate, Ada — that helps. Internal notes and action: 

- GL mapping: use 1325 (AR - WHT Receivable) for the SGD 2,853 and do not create a credit memo against revenue. This preserves recognized revenue and prevents revenue reclassification.
- Once we have bank proof of BrightWave remitting to the tax authority and the formal certificate (we have the certificate attached from Ada), we will:  
    • Clear the WHT receivable (1325) via a journal entry and move to 1540 (Tax Recoverable) if our tax team confirms we can claim a foreign tax credit; otherwise, write to 6205 (Other expense) if non-recoverable.
- AR aging: mark invoice RW-20270429 as paid (aged 0) in the cash-applied view; maintain separate suspense bucket for WHT so collections reporting doesn't double count.

Irene — can you approve the journal entry below so Marcus can post?

Proposed journal (to post after clearing with tax counsel):
Dr 1325 WHT Receivable SGD 2,853
Cr 1540 Tax Recoverable / or 6205 Other Expense SGD 2,853

If tax counsel confirms creditable, we'll choose 1540. Marcus — please coordinate posting and notify reporting so monthly AR metrics exclude the WHT bucket from outstanding DSO.

Cheers,
